newsitem.title: USA: Musicland shares slip on Moody's downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Musicland shares slip on Moody's downgrade.

text.p: Musicland Stores Corp shares dropped Friday afternoon after Moody's Investors Service Inc lowered its ratings on the company's senior subordinated notes, leading some industry analysts to speculate that the company may file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

The Moody's downgrade, to Ca from Caa, puts Musicland's debt in junk status. It followed a similar move by Standard & Poor's Corp that lowered Musicland's subordinated debt to triple-C-minus from single-B.
"Within three months, it's likely they will file (for Chapter 11), whether current management wants to or not," said Craig Bibb, an analyst at PaineWebber.
"The board is going to have to step in if the current management continues to avoid a Chapter 11 filing," Bibb said. "I think we'll have an answer on the Chapter 11 question by the end of March."
"The company has not filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection," Beth Heming, a Musicland spokeswoman, told Reuters.
The Minneapolis-based retailer is scheduled to begin repaying its bank debt at the end of March and has said it is working with Smith Barney on exploring its stratgic options.
Heming said the effort with Smith Barney continues.
Musicland is also reportedly working with its vendors, mostly major record labels, to defer scheduled payments with an option to convert the amounts due into an equity stake.
Heming declined to comment on these talks.
Heming said Musicland does not respond to ratings changes.
Another analyst said he believes the company will probably not file for bankruptcy.

"A Chapter 11 filing is unlikely in the near future," Edward White, an analyst at M.J. Whitman & Co, said. "Of course it's possible, but unlikely. All of the parties would be hurt by a Chapter 11 filing."
White added that Musicland will most likely try to renegotiate its bank loan agreements.

"They need new covenants, we've always known that," he said. "The bank loans are not secured so they'd be crazy to put the company in Chapter 11. I would be surprised if all of the parties don't find a way (to address liquidity problems)."

Musicland, which operates more than 770 mall-based music stores and 400 video stores, has closed 52 stores nationwide since December. The company's financial position has eroded in the last year because of continued weak sales.
White added there is another factor that may prevent a bankruptcy filing.
"Management owns about 12 percent of the stock," he said, "so it's working its tail off to avoid a Chapter 11 filing."
Musicland shares closed down 3/16 Friday at 15/16.
